correctness.rationale: For iid Bin(n,p) samples, exact CDF powers yield the maximal count PGF. The degree-two discriminant is nonnegative (strict for sample size at least two) by strict convexity. For every higher n, scaling the small-p PGF gives \(m(1+t)^n-(m-1)\), which has a simple nonreal root and transfers via root continuity. For n=3,m=2, a complete exact cubic discriminant factorization gives a strictly increasing threshold polynomial and hence the iff law. The bundled checker recomputed the cubic discriminant as an integer-polynomial identity and passed 2615 exact finite/algebraic checks. No finite enumeration is used to establish the infinite quantifiers.

value.rationale: Independent-Bernoulli representation enables exact factorized probability computations, PF/strongly Rayleigh consequences, and distributional inequalities. The natural operation of taking discrete maxima is known to preserve only ultra log-concavity. The theorem finds the largest binomial support parameter n permitting Bernoulli-factor preservation uniformly for arbitrary sample sizes, proves its failure in every larger dimension, and determines the complete success-probability boundary at the smallest failing dimension and sample size. This is a structural and exact parameter classification, not an isolated finite counterexample or arbitrary numerical slice.
